Subject: FuelMed discovery follow-up: sample data and high-level goals

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo and the useful discussion today. A quick recap from our side and the files I attached: a redacted sample (fuelmed_sample_dataset.csv) with patient-facing symptom descriptions and the desired canonical outcome label. Our primary goals are:
- fast triage suggestions (categorization into 6 buckets)
- free-text suggestion for next steps (1-2 sentence caregiver guidance)
- minimal hallucination on medication names and contraindications

Attaching the sample CSV and a short list of edge cases we want considered.

Questions for Redwood: what model families do you recommend for an initial pilot focused on precision over recall? What does an evaluation run look like on Redwood (dataset format, scoring criteria, turnaround)? Also send any example prompt sets you recommend for fine-grained intent/slot extraction.

Samir (CC) and I will prepare a larger anonymized export if the format matches your requirements.

Best,
Nina Patel
Head of Product
FuelMed

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-30T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FuelMed discovery follow-up: sample data and high-level goals

Nina — thanks for the sample and the clear goals. Good call today. Below is a short post-call recap and proposed next steps for the pilot + scoring approach.

Post-call recap (high level)
- Objective: 3-week model-fit pilot measuring categorical triage accuracy + free-text suggestion quality for 6 target buckets.
- Success criteria: baseline categorical precision >= 88% on a held-out set; free-text BLEU/ROUGE-style proxies + human spot checks (target: >85% accept rate).
- Data: fuelmed_sample_dataset.csv received; will need a full ~2k labeled rows for the pilot (redacted/anonymized).

Recommended models for pilot (initial):
- redwood-2.1-medium (production-grade, best latency/quality balance)
- open-llama-13b-q4 (if you need larger-context nuance; costlier)
- redwood-2.1-small (fast baseline to validate prompts and scoring)

Evaluation plan (short):
1) Dataset format: CSV with columns: id, text, label (bucket), gold_suggestion. For free-text ranking we also accept JSONL where each line is {"id","text","label","gold_suggestion"} — we can ingest both, but CSV preferred.
2) Scoring criteria:
   - Categorical: precision/recall/F1 by bucket; macro-averaged precision will be primary metric.
   - Free-text: automated metrics (BLEU/ROUGE) + a 200-sample human accept-rate (binary accept/reject) using scoring_matrix_v1.xlsx scheme.
   - Safety checks: hallucination rate on medication entities (NER-based false-positive rate) and exact-match for critical entities.
3) Run cadence: Redwood will run 3 model variants in parallel, return token-level latency, cost estimate, and the detailed scorecard. Typical turnaround ~48–72 hours after dataset handoff.

Attachments included: scoring_matrix_v1.xlsx, prompt_bank_v1.txt (starter prompts we discussed).

Immediate next steps
- Nina: share anonymized ~2k export in the CSV schema above by 2027-04-05.
- Redwood (Ben/Marissa): we will provide the formal pilot playbook, an S3 upload link + ingestion instructions, and a proposed kickoff slot.
- Procurement: CC in to confirm any NDA/Docs needed.

If this looks good I’ll lock a 45-minute kickoff on Mon 2027-04-05 (Calendly link below).

Cheers,
Logan Wright
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
https://calendly.com/logan-wright/fuelmed-kickoff
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Pilot ops + technical scoring notes (FuelMed)

On Tue, Mar 30, 2027 at 09:08 AM Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Nina — thanks for the sample and the clear goals. Good call today. Below is a short post-call recap and proposed next steps for the pilot + scoring approach.

Hi all — quick technical follow-up with the concrete eval/run steps we’ll use on Redwood and a few scoring clarifications.

1) Ingestion and formats - We will provide a pre-signed S3 bucket for the pilot upload. CSV should be UTF-8, newline separated, with header row: id,text,label,gold_suggestion. If you need to include multiple gold suggestions per id, use a JSONL where gold_suggestion is an array string.

2) Evaluation harness (how Redwood runs it) - We run each model variant against the test partition and produce: prediction.csv (id,pred_label,pred_suggestion,confidence,latency_ms).
- Command (internal shorthand): redwood eval run --dataset s3://redwood-pilot/fuelmed/2027-04- --models redwood-2.1-medium,redwood-2.1-small,open-llama-13b-q4 --scorer scoring_matrix_v1.xlsx

3) Scoring specifics - Categorical: we’ll compute per-bucket precision/recall and macro precision as primary KPI.
- Free-text: automated similarity (embedding cosine + ROUGE) and canonicalization rules (strip stop tokens, canonicalize med names via provided dictionary).

4) Safety/quality regression guardrails - We’ll run an entity-exactness test for medication/care-critical entities. If hallucination rate >2% on medicinals we trigger alert and rollout freeze. Historical baseline: model redwood-2.1-medium shows ~1.1% medication hallucinations on similar triage datasets.

5) Human-in-the-loop review - For the pilot we recommend 200 human reviews sampled stratified by bucket. We’ll provide the audit UI and scoring rubric; results feed back into a small calibration run.

6) Model recommendations rationale - Start with redwood-2.1-medium as the primary variant (balance latency/cost/quality). If you need more nuanced free-text, run open-llama-13b-q4 as an experimental variant and compare acceptance rates.

7) Deliverables and timeline - Redwood to deliver run results + scorecard and recommended model config within 72 hours of dataset upload.

Action items (technical)
- Redwood: share S3 pre-signed location and upload instructions (Ben) — by 2027-04-01.
- FuelMed: deliver anonymized ~2k CSV following schema by 2027-04-05 (Nina/Samir).
- Redwood: schedule pilot kickoff and assign scorer pool for HTR (Marissa).

Attachment: scoring_matrix_v1.xlsx (column definitions and human rubric)

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick technical sync if you want to walk through the scoring matrix.

Ben Carter
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
